title: Wedjat capacity-sign paleography: primary-source candidate ledger before sign scoring
purpose: Identify institutional, dated textual witnesses and controls before inspecting or scoring whether capacity-submultiple sign forms resemble proposed Wedjat components.

primary_witness_candidates.institutional_description: Mathematics textbook-like papyrus including eighty-four problems with divisions, multiplications, fractions, areas and volumes; dated by scribe Ahmose to year 33 of Apophis.
Second museum section of the same Rhind Mathematical Papyrus, attributed to scribe Ahmose and containing mathematical problems including fractions.
primary_witness_candidates.independence_warning: Do not count EA10057 and EA10058 as two independent ancient documents.

primary_witness_candidates.institutional_description: Fragments separated from the main Rhind roll; upper fragments come from the end of a section dealing with simplification of fractions and lower fragments from bread-division material.
primary_witness_candidates.independence_warning: Useful as additional physical/facsimile evidence, not an independent document from the British Museum Rhind sections.

primary_witness_candidates.institutional_description: Independent 2:n fraction-reckoning table showing n=3 to n=21; UCL notes that its unit-fraction decompositions are exactly the same as the corresponding Rhind table entries.
Calculations for two problems, including a granary-volume problem parallel to Rhind problem 43 and a ration problem parallel to Rhind problem 64.
Mathematical fragment with the title 'Method of calculating the matters of accounting' and two problems.
Accounts recording deliveries in hekats from farmers and distribution of barley rations.
Letter concerning barley quantities including 20 hekats, 1 hekat, 2 hekats and a one-quarter quantity in the surviving translation.
Institutional index to multiple independent business/account papyri from Lahun, including grain accounts and produce records with photographs/transcriptions for selected objects.

new_controls.same_document_fragment_control: British Museum EA10057, EA10058 and Brooklyn 37.1784Ea-b belong to the Rhind-document lineage and must not be treated as independent replication.
new_controls.fraction_notation_control: Lahun UC32159 independently preserves ordinary unit-fraction table notation. Any proposed eye-specific morphology must outperform generic fraction-sign morphology from the same scribal culture.
new_controls.domain_transfer_control: UC32110B and UC32214 place hekat quantities in practical accounts/letters, allowing comparison of capacity notation outside a mathematical textbook context if target fractional signs are visibly present.
new_controls.scribal_style_control: Use non-target signs from the same line/document matched for stroke count and aspect ratio when scoring resemblance to Wedjat components.

important_result_of_source_discovery: A viable primary-source path exists beyond one modern diagram: the Rhind manuscript has institutional object and image records, its separated fragments are independently catalogued by Brooklyn Museum, and the earlier Lahun corpus provides multiple independent mathematical and practical-account witnesses. However, target capacity-submultiple sign occurrences have not yet been localized and therefore no paleographic similarity result is admitted.
next_gate: Download legally available institutional images or facsimiles, SHA-256 seal them before target inspection, then localize fractional-hekat/capacity-submultiple occurrences by edition locator. Count physical documents, not museum frames, for replication. Expand the Lahun account pool until at least 12 genuinely independent documents with target-sign evidence or matched negative controls are frozen.
